question: Who among the following has written the book ‘The God of Small Things’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arundhati Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Arundhati Roy is the author of the book 'The God of Small Things'.
 
• Roy's debut novel, it is a story about the childhood experiences of fraternal twins whose lives are destroyed by the "Love Laws" prevalent in 1960s Kerala, India. 
 
• The novel explores how small, seemingly insignificant things shape people's behavior and their lives.
 
• The novel also explores the lingering effects of casteism in India.
 
• It won the Booker Prize in 1997.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **R. K. Narayan **was an Indian writer, who has written Malgudi days.

 
 
• He becomes the main creator of early Indian literature in English in conjunction with Mulk Raj Anand and Raja Rao.
 
• Some of his books are Swami and Friends, Bachelor of Arts, The English Teacher.
 
• In 1960, he was awarded Sahitya Akademi Award for his novel The Guide.
 
 
 
• Salman Rushdie:
 
 
• He is a British-American novelist and essayist of Indian descent.
 
• He won the Booker Prize in 1981 for his novel *Midnight's Children.*
 
• His book *The Satanic Verses *came into a lot of controversies.
 
 
 
• Amitav Ghosh was born on July 11, 1956, in Kolkata. He received a B.A. degree in 1976 and an M.A. in 1978 from the University of Delhi.
 
 
• Amitav Ghosh is an Indian writer and the winner of the 54th Jnanpith award, best known for his work in English fiction.
 
• He won the Jnanpith award for his contribution to the enrichment of Indian literature in English in 2019.
 
• His first novel was "The Circle of Reason" published in the year 1986.
 
• Ghosh's works include-** The Circle of Reason (his 1986 debut novel), The Shadow Lines (1988), The Glass Palace (2000), The Hungry Tide (2004), and Sea of Poppies (2008), the first volume of The Ibis trilogy, set in the 1830s just before the Opium War and encapsulating the East's colonial history.**
